en: Never leave your studies for the last minute.
tamil: படிப்பை எப்பவும் கடைசி நிமிஷத்துக்கு விட்டுடாதே.
explain: 'Never' + verb is a strong negative command. 'Last minute' means at the end.
usage: Use it as advice for a junior or your own children.
leelaQ: Do you finish your work early or at the last minute?
answer: I try to finish early, but sometimes I am late.

en: Take a five minute break and then continue studying.
tamil: ஐந்து நிமிஷம் ஓய்வு எடுத்துட்டு அப்புறம் படிப்பை தொடரு.
context: Advising a friend who looks tired.
explain: 'Take a break' is a fixed phrase. 'Then' joins the next action.
usage: Use it with a friend or a child who has studied for long.
leelaQ: What do you do in a short break?
answer: I drink tea and walk for a few minutes.

en: I joined an evening class to improve my spoken English.
tamil: என் பேச்சு இங்கிலீஷை மேம்படுத்த நான் ஒரு ஈவ்னிங் கிளாஸ்ல சேர்ந்தேன்.
context: Telling someone why you started a class.
explain: 'To improve' gives the purpose. 'Spoken English' means speaking skill.
usage: Use it when friends ask why you go out every evening.
leelaQ: Why do you want to improve your English?
answer: I want a better job and more confidence.

en: Is the project deadline this Friday?
tamil: ப்ராஜெக்ட் டெட்லைன் இந்த வெள்ளிக்கிழமையா?
explain: A question with 'is' can be answered with yes or no.
usage: Use it with team members or the guide to avoid confusion.
leelaQ: How do you manage a deadline?
answer: I split the work into small parts and finish one each day.

en: We will have a revision test on Monday.
tamil: எங்களுக்கு திங்கள்கிழமை ஒரு ரிவிஷன் டெஸ்ட் இருக்கு.
explain: 'Will have' is used for planned events. 'On' goes with days.
usage: Use it to remind classmates or children about the next test.
leelaQ: What day is the hardest for you in a week?
answer: Monday is hardest because I wake up late.

en: She teaches maths in a government school.
tamil: அவங்க அரசு பள்ளியில கணக்கு பாடம் எடுக்குறாங்க.
context: Introducing a teacher to a guest.
explain: 'Teaches' takes -es after 'she'. 'In a school' tells the workplace.
usage: Use it when you tell someone about a relative's job.
leelaQ: What does your family do for a living?
answer: My father is a farmer and my mother is a teacher.

en: What did you score in the unit test?
tamil: யூனிட் டெஸ்ட்ல நீ எவ்வளவு மார்க் வாங்கின?
context: Asking a friend after the results.
explain: 'Score' is used for marks. 'Did' makes the past question.
usage: Use it casually with classmates after marks are given.
leelaQ: Are you happy with your marks?
answer: Yes, I am happy because I studied well.

en: Small goals make a big study plan easy to follow.
tamil: சின்ன இலக்குகள் பெரிய படிப்பு திட்டத்தை பின்பற்ற சுலபமாக்கும்.
explain: 'Make something easy' means to cause it to become easy.
usage: Use it when you guide a younger student or a learner.
leelaQ: What small goal can you set for this week?
answer: I will learn five new words every day.

en: Please help me prepare for tomorrow's presentation.
tamil: நாளைய ப்ரசன்டேஷனுக்கு நான் தயாராக உதவுங்க.
context: Asking a friend or a senior.
explain: 'Help me + verb' is a common pattern. 'Tomorrow's' is the possessive form.
usage: Use it with a senior or a friend who is good at speaking.
leelaQ: Who helps you when you have an important task?
answer: My friend helps me with ideas and practice.

en: The headmaster announced the exam dates this morning.
tamil: ஹெட்மாஸ்டர் இன்னைக்கு காலையில தேர்வு தேதிகளை அறிவிச்சாரு.
context: Sharing school news with a parent.
explain: 'Announced' means told everyone officially. 'This morning' is a past time.
usage: Use it with a parent or a friend when the exam schedule is out.
leelaQ: Which exam date worries you the most?
answer: The maths exam worries me the most.

en: I wasn't able to finish the syllabus on time.
tamil: என்னால சிலபஸை நேரத்துக்கு முடிக்க முடியல.
explain: 'Wasn't able to' is a past form of 'can't'. 'On time' means by the correct time.
usage: Use it when you explain to a parent or a teacher why you did not do well.
leelaQ: What stops you from finishing your work on time?
answer: Too many other jobs stop me from finishing.

en: Are you going to attend the extra class on Sunday?
tamil: நீ ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமை எக்ஸ்ட்ரா கிளாஸுக்கு வரப் போறியா?
explain: 'Attend' is used for classes and events. 'Going to' asks about the plan.
usage: Use it to check with a friend if they will come for a special class.
leelaQ: How do you spend your Sundays?
answer: I rest, do my laundry, and watch a movie.

en: I will join a coaching centre after my twelfth.
tamil: நான் பன்னிரண்டாம் வகுப்புக்கு அப்புறம் ஒரு கோச்சிங் சென்டர்ல சேருவேன்.
context: Telling a relative your future plan.
explain: 'After my twelfth' is common Indian English for after class 12.
usage: Use it when relatives ask what you plan after school.
leelaQ: What will you do after your studies?
answer: I will look for a job in a software company.

en: Our lab assistant showed us how to use the microscope.
tamil: எங்க லேப் அசிஸ்டென்ட் மைக்ரோஸ்கோப்பை எப்படி பயன்படுத்தணும்னு காட்டினாரு.
explain: 'Showed us how to + verb' explains a demonstration.
usage: Use it when you tell a parent about what you did in the lab.
leelaQ: What was the most interesting class you ever had?
answer: The most interesting class was a science experiment.

en: Do you prefer studying alone or in a group?
tamil: நீ தனியா படிக்கிறதை விரும்புவியா இல்ல குரூப்பாவா?
explain: 'Prefer' is followed by -ing. 'Or' gives two choices.
usage: Use it with new friends to learn about their study style.
leelaQ: Why do you prefer that way?
answer: I prefer it because I can focus better.

en: Let us make a study plan for this month.
tamil: இந்த மாசத்துக்கு ஒரு படிப்பு திட்டம் போடலாம்.
explain: 'Let us' invites someone to do something together.
usage: Use it with a friend or a sibling to start planning together.
leelaQ: What is one thing you want to finish this month?
answer: I want to finish a small online course this month.

en: I am doing my MBA through distance education.
tamil: நான் தொலைதூர கல்வி மூலமா என் எம்பிஏ படிச்சிட்டு இருக்கேன்.
explain: 'Through' shows the method. 'Am doing' shows a longer ongoing task.
usage: Use it with colleagues when you work and study together.
leelaQ: Do you want to study more while working?
answer: Yes, I want to do a course on weekends.

en: I have booked my seat for the entrance exam.
tamil: நான் நுழைவுத் தேர்வுக்கு என் இடத்தை பதிவு பண்ணிட்டேன்.
explain: 'Have booked' shows the work is done and ready now. 'Entrance exam' tests you to enter a college.
usage: Use it when your friends ask about the exam registration.
leelaQ: Have you registered for any exam recently?
answer: Yes, I registered for a typing test last month.

en: Why are you learning Angular?
tamil: நீ ஏன் ஆங்குலர் கத்துக்கிட்டு இருக்க?
context: A friend asks about your new skill.
explain: 'Why' asks for a reason. Answer with 'because' or 'to'.
usage: Use it with a colleague or a friend who is starting a new course.
leelaQ: What do you want to build with it?
answer: I want to build a small app for practising English.

en: Every Saturday, we have a small quiz in class.
tamil: ஒவ்வொரு சனிக்கிழமையும் நாங்க கிளாஸ்ல ஒரு சின்ன க்விஸ் வைப்போம்.
explain: 'Every Saturday' at the start shows a regular habit.
usage: Use it to explain your weekly class routine to a new friend.
leelaQ: Do you enjoy quizzes?
answer: Yes, I enjoy them because they make learning fun.

en: There is no need to panic before the exam.
tamil: பரீட்சைக்கு முன்னாடி பயப்பட வேண்டிய அவசியம் இல்ல.
explain: 'There is no need to + verb' means it is not necessary. It sounds calm and kind.
usage: Use it to calm a nervous friend or a child before a test.
leelaQ: How do you stay calm before a big day?
answer: I take deep breaths and do a short walk.

en: Could you share the link for the online class?
tamil: ஆன்லைன் கிளாஸுக்கான லிங்கை பகிர முடியுமா?
context: Messaging a teacher or a group.
explain: 'Share the link' is a normal phrase for online classes.
usage: Use it in a class group chat when you cannot find the class link.
leelaQ: Do you prefer online classes or classroom classes?
answer: I prefer classroom classes because I can ask questions easily.

en: My friend helped me with the maths problems.
tamil: என் நண்பன் கணக்கு பிரச்சனைகள்ல எனக்கு உதவி பண்ணான்.
explain: 'Helped me with' is followed by a thing. 'Problems' here means sums.
usage: Use it when someone asks how you solved a tough sum.
leelaQ: Who helps you when you are stuck?
answer: My elder sister helps me when I am stuck.

en: Have you chosen a topic for your presentation?
tamil: உன் ப்ரசன்டேஷனுக்கு ஒரு தலைப்பு தேர்ந்தெடுத்துட்டியா?
explain: 'Have you chosen' asks about a decision already made.
usage: Use it with a classmate before a seminar.
leelaQ: What topic would you like to talk about?
answer: I would like to talk about my favourite cricketer.

en: Reading the question paper carefully saves a lot of mistakes.
tamil: கேள்வித்தாளை கவனமா படிக்கிறது நிறைய தவறுகளை தவிர்க்கும்.
explain: 'Carefully' tells how to read. 'Saves mistakes' means avoids them.
usage: Use it when you advise juniors or your children before an exam.
leelaQ: What do you do first when you get a question paper?
answer: I read all the questions once before I start.
